t: A tiny RISC-V Linux board with a camera connector and a small AI helper.
steps: Look for remaining stock from Milk-V agents such as ARACE. The board launched at about 9 US dollars. The Duo 256M is its newer sibling.
Get a microSD card and a USB-C cable with a 5 volt 1 amp supply.
Download the Duo Linux image from the Milk-V docs and write it to the card.
Insert the card, plug in USB-C and log in from your computer.
Blink the onboard LED with the Linux example in the getting started guide.
Install the Arduino IDE and add the Milk-V Duo board package.
Upload the Blink sketch to run on the small core.
